# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

messages.content:
TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🫵 👆 👇 🤝 ☝ 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤟 👈]

**Thinking:**
I am Deaf. I can see the bomb and gestures, but I cannot hear speech or read the manual directly (though Mute is trying to communicate). I also cannot touch the bomb.

The Bomb State:
- Display: 0
- Light: Green
- Button: Large, labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE"
- Wires: 1:Green, 2:Yellow, 3:Red

Mute's Gesture: `[✋ 🫵 👆 👇 🤝 ☝ 👎]`
Blind's Gesture: `[👉 🤟 👈]`

Since I cannot speak (or rather, my speech isn't heard by anyone if I'm Deaf? Wait, the rules say "You are shown your own share... You each hold a different piece". The roles are fixed. Deaf sees, Mute reads manual, Blind touches.
Deaf *can* speak. "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So my words will be heard by them.
Deaf *can* gesture. "When you gesture, Mute receives it." Blind cannot see gestures.

Let's interpret the context. Usually, these puzzles follow standard logic.
If the light is GREEN, often that means safe or specific wire cutting.
"PUSH TO DEFUSE" is on the button. Is it a trap? Or is it the solution?
Wires: Green, Yellow, Red.

Mute's gesture sequence is complex. `✋` (Stop/Hand), `🫵` (You), `👆` (Up/First?), `👇` (Down/Last?), `🤝` (Together/Link?), `☝` (One/Index), `👎` (Bad/No).
This looks like instructions for who does what.
Maybe: Stop. You (Blind?) Up? Down? Link? One? No?

Blind's gesture: `👉` (Right/Point Right), `🤟` (Love/Rock?), `👈` (Left/Point Left).
This might indicate direction of wires or position.

However, I need to send information to Blind so they can act. Blind cannot see the colors. I must tell Blind which wire to cut or what to do with the button.
Standard bomb defusal tropes:
- If there is a red wire and no yellow wire, cut the second wire from the right.
- If there is a blue wire but no red wire, cut the first wire.
- If there are more than two wires and all are yellow, cut the last wire.
- If there are exactly two wires and both are yellow, cut the last wire.
- Otherwise, cut the first wire.

But here we have Green, Yellow, Red. And a "Push to Defuse" button.
Often, "Push to Defuse" is a lie/trap unless conditions are met.
Or maybe the green light indicates it's safe to push?

Let's look at Mute's gesture again. It's likely translating the Manual.
If I assume the manual says something about the button vs wires.
Without hearing Mute's speech (which doesn't exist for me anyway) or seeing the manual, I have to rely on the visual state.

Visual State:
Light: Green.
Button: Present.
Wires: G, Y, R.

Hypothesis 1: The Green Light means the button is active/safe.
Hypothesis 2: The wires need to be cut in a specific order based on color.

Let's try to communicate the most critical info to Blind. Blind needs to know the colors and positions.
Wire 1: Green
Wire 2: Yellow
Wire 3: Red

If I tell Blind to cut Wire 2 (Yellow), does that make sense?
In many games, if there is a green light, you don't cut wires, you press the button. Or vice versa.

Let's look at Blind's gesture: `👉 🤟 👈`. This could mean "Look left/right" or "Cut middle"? Or "Don't touch"?
Mute's gesture ends with `👎` (Bad/No). Maybe "Don't push button"?

If "Don't push button", then we must cut wires.
Which wire?
Common rule: Cut the red wire if it's not connected to anything else? No.
Common rule: Cut the wire matching the light color? Light is Green. Wire 1 is Green.

Let's assume the instruction is to cut the wire that matches the light color.
So, cut Wire 1 (Green).

I will instruct Blind to cut the first wire (the one closest to the left/start, usually Wire 1).
I need to describe the wire clearly. "Cut the green wire."
Blind can feel the insulation color? Usually, blind characters in these puzzles are told the color by the seer.

Let's formulate the message.
To Blind: "Do not push the button. Cut the green wire (Wire 1)."

Wait, I should check if I can verify this with Mute.
Mute is gesturing to me. I can't ask Mute questions easily because I can't hear their reply if they spoke, but I can see their next turn's gestures.
But I have to act now.

Let's look at the gestures again.
Mute: `✋` (Stop). `🫵` (You - pointing at me?). `👆` (Up/First). `👇` (Down/Last). `🤝` (Together). `☝` (One). `👎` (No/Bad).
This is very ambiguous without a key.

Blind: `👉` (Right). `🤟` (Rock/Love). `👈` (Left).
Could mean "Not Left, Not Right"? Middle?
If Blind points Left and Right, maybe indicating the outer wires are bad? Leaving the middle (Yellow)?

If I combine "Middle wire" (from Blind's potential hint about sides being wrong) and "Green Light" (Safe?):
Maybe cut the middle wire? Wire 2 (Yellow).

Let's try a safer bet. The button says "PUSH TO DEFUSE". The light is GREEN. In many simple logic puzzles, Green Light + Button = Push Button.
BUT, Mute's gesture ended with `👎` (Thumbs down). This strongly suggests "NO" to something. If the obvious action is pushing the button, the thumbs down likely means "DO NOT PUSH THE BUTTON".

So, we must cut a wire.
Blind's gesture `👉 ... 👈` might imply "Ignore the sides" or "It's between them".
This points to Wire 2 (Yellow).

Also, common trope: If light is green, cut the non-green wire? Or cut the green wire?
If I cut the green wire (matching light), that's a common rule.
If I cut the middle wire, that's another common rule ("Otherwise cut the first" etc, but "middle" is less common as a default).

Let's look at Wire Colors: Green, Yellow, Red.
If the rule was "Cut the red wire if...", well, Red is Wire 3.
If the rule was "Cut the yellow wire...", Yellow is Wire 2.

Let's assume Blind's gesture `👉 🤟 👈` means "Left and Right are bad/wrong, choose the other/middle".
And Mute's `👎` means "Don't push button".

So: Don't push button. Cut the middle wire (Yellow).

I will send this to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Do not push the button. Cut the middle wire. It is yellow.")
```
